title: TailLoR: Protecting Principal Components in Parameter-Efficient Continual Learning
abstract: Parameter-efficient finetuning methods based on spectral decomposition have enabled progress in Continual Learning. In this paper we introduce TailLoR, which utilizes the singular bases U and V of the pre-trained weights as a fixed reference frame to learn a low-rank update applied to the singular value matrix. A soft spectral penalty discourages updates aligned with dominant singular directions, reducing interference while routing fine-grained adaptation into the highly flexible, long-tail spectral coordinates.

significance.justification: The paper refines a known technique (spectral decomposition for parameter-efficient finetuning) by introducing a soft spectral penalty to reduce interference in continual learning, offering measurable gains for builders implementing continual learning systems.

novelty.justification: The method presents a substantial new variation by using singular bases as a fixed reference frame and applying a soft penalty to protect principal components, a distinct approach from prior low-rank adaptation techniques.

reproducibility.justification: The method is described clearly enough to reimplement, as the paper details the use of singular bases and a spectral penalty, but no mention is made of public code, weights, or datasets.

clarity.justification: The abstract is solidly written, clearly presenting the problem (interference in continual learning), the proposed solution (TailLoR), and its core mechanism (soft spectral penalty on dominant singular directions).

topical_fit.justification: The paper is clearly in scope, addressing parameter-efficient finetuning and continual learning for pre-trained models, which are central concerns for engineers building and adapting LLM systems.
